context:
Follow existing patterns from test_release_sync.py: class-based grouping, tmp_path fixture for
filesystem operations, direct imports from benchbox.release modules.

All tests marked @pytest.mark.fast (no real builds, no network, no real git operations). The
conftest auto-marker in tests/conftest.py automatically applies 'fast' to tests in tests/unit/,
so explicit markers are optional but recommended for clarity.

Mock subprocess.run for git/build operations. Mock datetime.now() for deterministic weekday tests.
Create zip files with zipfile.ZipFile for wheel verification tests (no real uv build).

For script function tests, add scripts/ to sys.path via either:
- A conftest.py fixture in tests/unit/ that inserts scripts/ path
- Or direct sys.path manipulation at top of test_release_scripts.py
The scripts already do sys.path.insert(0, ...) for their own imports, so this mirrors that pattern.

Import strategy for each test file:
- test_release_fingerprint.py: from benchbox.release.workflow import compute_source_fingerprint
- test_release_timestamps.py: from benchbox.release.workflow import calculate_most_recent_saturday_midnight, _normalize_timestamps
- test_content_validation.py: from benchbox.release.content_validation import validate_file, validate_content, check_content_for_release, ContentViolation, ValidationResult, Severity, _is_example_line, _has_inline_ignore, _get_context, _should_skip_file, _get_file_exceptions, RULE_CATEGORIES
- test_release_size_check.py: from benchbox.release.workflow import check_release_size, ReleaseSizeViolation, ALLOWED_DATA_PATHS, FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS, DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB, DEFAULT_MAX_TOTAL_SIZE_MB
- test_release_scripts.py: import parse_timestamp, run_pre_flight_checks, run_ci_checks from automate_release; calculate_sha256, verify_wheel_timestamps from build_release; verify_wheel_fingerprint from verify_release; git_commit_with_timestamp, git_tag_with_timestamp, verify_git_status, archive_release_artifacts, verify_source_fingerprint from finalize_release
description:
The release automation system is sophisticated (~3,000 lines across benchbox/release/workflow.py,
benchbox/release/content_validation.py, and 5 scripts) but significantly under-tested. Existing
tests (test_release_infrastructure.py, test_release_sync.py) cover repo metadata, YAML validation,
version consistency, and sync functions -- but zero coverage exists for source fingerprinting,
timestamp normalization, content validation, size safety checks, and release script functions.

These are critical-path components that prevent source/artifact divergence, ensure reproducible
builds, and gate releases. A fingerprinting bug could ship mismatched artifacts; a timestamp
normalization bug could leak build times; a size check gap could allow multi-GB data files into
releases.

This TODO adds ~160 test cases across 5 new test files, organized into 4 phases by dependency
order (fingerprinting is foundational, scripts depend on understanding the functions they wrap).

anti_patterns.dont: create integration tests that require git repos or network
anti_patterns.instead: mock subprocess.run for all git operations
anti_patterns.why: these are unit tests that must run fast and offline

anti_patterns.dont: import scripts using importlib or exec() hacks
anti_patterns.instead: mirror that pattern with a simple sys.path.insert in the test file
anti_patterns.why: scripts already use sys.path.insert for their own imports

anti_patterns.dont: modify any production code to make it more testable
anti_patterns.instead: test the interfaces as they exist
anti_patterns.why: these are public interfaces that should be tested as-is

anti_patterns.dont: run real 'uv build' in unit tests
anti_patterns.instead: use zipfile.ZipFile to create fake wheel archives instead
anti_patterns.why: builds take 10+ seconds and require full toolchain

anti_patterns.instead: use tmp_path and mocks to keep everything fast
anti_patterns.why: all these tests should complete in <30s total

preserves.behavior: All existing tests in tests/ continue passing
No modifications to production code in benchbox/release/ or scripts/
